events.title: Girolamo Savonarola Burned at the Stake
events.description: The Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola, who had ruled Florence as a theocratic reformer after the expulsion of the Medici, was hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria after being excommunicated and convicted of heresy and sedition.
events.significance: His execution ended a radical experiment in religious republican rule in Florence and showed the power of the papacy and political rivals over reformist movements before the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Defenestration of Prague
events.description: Protestant nobles in Bohemia threw two Catholic Imperial governors and their secretary out of a window of Prague Castle in protest against the religious policies of Habsburg Emperor Matthias and Ferdinand II.
events.significance: The incident triggered the Bohemian Revolt and is widely regarded as the start of the Thirty Years' War, one of the deadliest conflicts in European history.

events.title: Federal Republic of Germany Established
events.description: The Basic Law (Grundgesetz) was promulgated in Bonn, founding West Germany as a democratic federal state in the American, British, and French occupation zones after World War II.
events.significance: The founding of West Germany formalized the division of Germany during the Cold War and laid the foundation for a stable democracy that later reunified with East Germany in 1990.

events.title: Bonnie and Clyde Killed in Ambush
events.description: Outlaws Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were killed by a posse of law enforcement officers in an ambush near Sailes, Louisiana, ending a two-year crime spree across the central United States during the Great Depression.
events.significance: Their deaths marked a milestone in the 'public enemy' era of American crime and the rise of federal and coordinated law enforcement, and their story became a lasting part of popular culture.

events.title: Birth of Carl Linnaeus
events.description: Carl Linnaeus, the Swedish naturalist who formalized binomial nomenclature, was born in Råshult, Småland, Sweden.
events.significance: Linnaeus's system of naming and classifying organisms became the foundation of modern taxonomy and biological classification used worldwide.
